title: Runbook Graph Executor — permissioned, simulatable tasklets for safe ops
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: oncall engineers regularly run multi-step remediation playbooks that touch services in different clusters and require scoped privileges. Current runbooks are linear scripts or ad-hoc sequences; they are hard to review, hard to simulate, and frequently cause permission escalations or unexpected side effects during execution.

Goal: build a Runbook Graph Executor that compiles authored runbooks into an explicit DAG of idempotent tasklets with typed inputs, least-privilege execution tokens, and a simulated 'dry-run' execution mode. The executor must support: step-level concurrency controls, automatic rollback suggestions based on recent telemetry, and audit-proof provenance for each execution.

What we'll deliver: a server-side graph compiler + runtime that: (1) accepts runbook definitions (YAML/JSON) and produces a validated task graph; (2) performs a preflight simulation against a sandbox snapshot (no destructive calls) and emits a delta-risk score; (3) issues short-lived, scoped execution tokens (via KMS/SSO integration) to run only the exact steps required; (4) streams structured run events to the Console with rich links to traces/metrics for each node; (5) supports canary-targeting (play first on shadow cluster or single host) and automatic fallback to safe alternative steps if failure patterns match regression signatures.

Acceptance criteria:
- Graph compiler validates input schemas and rejects non-idempotent step definitions unless explicit acknowledgement label is present.
- Dry-run simulation returns per-step side-effect footprint and an overall risk score within <= 2s for graphs with <= 25 steps.
- Execution tokens are minted per-run with scoped RBAC and expire after run completion; audit log contains token fingerprint and KMS key ID.
- Console shows per-node telemetry (latency, error-rate, impacted endpoints) and a single-click ‘Abort & Rollback’ that triggers the compiled rollback path.
- Integration tests that run 50 representative real runbooks in a mirrored sandbox pass within CI with deterministic outputs.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- We will prefer an explicit DAG model (nodes + typed inputs + outputs) over a Turing-complete DSL to keep analysis tractable; this reduces expressivity but enables static analysis, sandboxing, and automatic rollback inference.
- Scoped tokens require changes in our IAM/KMS flow; short-term we will adopt a token proxy that mints ephemeral tokens via existing KMS integrations to avoid a full IAM overhaul.
- Dry-run fidelity: initial simulation will mock external effects and score risk heuristically (telemetry-based heuristics). True effectful dry-run (wire calls to canary infra) will be opt-in and gated behind environment flags.
- Concurrency scheduling: default is serial with optional parallel branches declared explicitly. We'll enforce a sane max-parallelism per run (configurable at org level).

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal-only runnable in lab; enable on the ops-sandbox with five pilot runbooks (Mar 2026).
2) Beta: enable for SREs and Customer Support in staged orgs; collect risk-score calibration telemetry and adjust heuristics (Apr 2026).
3) GA: enable org opt-in in Console with RBAC and audit retention tuning (May 2026).

Telemetry & monitoring:
- Emit structured events to tracing pipeline for each node: start/end timestamps, inputs, outputs (sanitized), error-class, KMS key ID.
- Track correlation between run failures and recent deployments, surface top-3 likely regression candidates.
- Add SLO: dry-run simulation and compile latency 95th <= 2s for graphs <=25 steps; execution event delivery success rate >= 99.9%.

Security & compliance:
- All run artifacts and logs encrypted at rest; KMS key ID recorded per run.
- Require manager approval for any run that includes steps marked 'high-impact' or out-of-org scope.
- Security review required before Beta (recorded in this ticket).

Docs & UX:
- API: /runs/compile, /runs/simulate, /runs/execute, /runs/{id}/rollback.
- Console: run builder UI that renders DAG, shows input types, dry-run button, mint-for-approval flow, and per-node fulltrace link.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- Graph compiler service (go) + validation layer (JSON schema).
- Dry-run simulation harness (python runner that mocks infra and scores risk).
- Scoped token proxy service (auth layer integrating with existing KMS flows).
- Console components: DAG visualizer, run builder, per-node telemetry stream.
- CI: sandbox fixtures and deterministic replay harness for 50 runbooks.

Notes on testing and observability: we will create a small benchmark corpus of 100 historical runbooks (sanitized) and measure false-positive risk scoring. We'll build replayable fixtures that pin telemetry traces so dry-run outputs are deterministic in CI.
